rationale: M60 R10 follow-up, the declared-reference half of the `scoped_type_identifier` gap. The lane already accepts a QUALIFIED type in its heritage path, its object-creation type node, its record-component extractor, its import edges and `baseTypeName` itself — whose doctrine is written in the source ('a scoped type keeps its full dotted text, matching the Java analyzer convention', and the java lane publishes `java.util.Map.Entry` for the same shape). The declared-reference collectors were the two places that did NOT: `collectTypeNames` and the two type-clause walks select with `type === "type_identifier"` or `endsWith("type")`/`endsWith("_type")`, and `scoped_type_identifier` ends in "identifier", so it matched neither. Measured before the fix (script/m14/tmp/groovy-scoped-type-ref-probe.ts): `Outer.Criterion qualifiedField` emitted NO edge while `Criterion leafField` emitted one — the qualified half of every declared-type position was simply absent from the graph, so a field, local, parameter, return type or coercion written with its qualifier contributed nothing to the type-usage graph. After the fix the qualified type is admitted as ONE type node — the full dotted text — and never descended into, which is what the negatives below state: its segments are package/class names, not types. The `forbidRelationships` list is the whole point of this fixture — an expect-only matcher cannot see a lane that emits BOTH the dotted name and its leaf, and it cannot see `java`, `util` and `Map` published as types either. Type ARGUMENTS stay their own types by design (`String` and `Boolean` are real declared types in `java.util.Map.Entry<String, Boolean>`), so they are pinned as present. Every edge carries the line the TYPE is spelled on rather than its declaration's opening line (the M59 #825 contract), which is why each want names a line. This fixture also states the as-coercion half, where the first authored expectation was wrong about `declaredOn` (`as_cast` is the inert legacy branch's marker; the shipped grammar's as-coercion is a `binary_expression`) — corrected to the measured value rather than to the analyzer's convenience.

expectRelationships.note: field position: the qualified type keeps its full dotted text
generic + qualified: the BASE keeps its qualifier
type ARGUMENTS are types in their own right and must keep being emitted

`as` coercion: the as-type node is reached through the same collector. declaredOn is the NODE KIND the type is declared on — groovy's as-coercion IS a binary_expression in the pinned grammar (probe-verified: binary_expression{left: identifier, operator: `as`, type: scoped_type_identifier}) — matching how the field/local positions report field_declaration / local_variable_declaration. AUTHORING CORRECTION: this want first said `as_cast`, which is the marker the lane's inert PRE-#742-rebuild branch emits (that branch is kept only for an older wasm and never runs against the shipped grammar). The analyzer was right and the expectation was wrong; the measured value is pinned instead, so the fixture records the live node kind rather than a marker from dead code.

CHANNEL pin for the return-type edge, deliberately with NO `source`. A method whose return type is QUALIFIED emits a `return_type` reference, and that label is load-bearing: the KAD6 regression relabels the whole edge to declared_type and re-sources it, losing information no re-attribution can absorb, so this row must go unmet when it happens. `source` is left unconstrained on purpose - the enclosing-type-vs-method attribution is the OPEN finding the rows above already report (they are unmet today), and pinning either side here would bury it. This row pins that the edge EXISTS and carries return_type; who owns it stays a separate, still-failing question.

CHANNEL pin for the `as`-coercion cast edge, deliberately with NO `source`. It is the ONLY edge in this fixture that can satisfy it, which makes it a loss detector for the whole cast_type channel (`o as String`, `[] as Set`, `x as T[]`, `(String) o`): if a regression stops emitting cast references, or reverts to the pre-#742 mis-parse marker, this row goes unmet. `source` stays unconstrained so the disputed attribution above keeps failing on its own.

forbidRelationships.note: the LEAF of a qualified type: a class segment is not a separately named type — the pre-fix descent emitted exactly this
the QUALIFIER alone is not a type reference
package segment — the class a name like collectTypeNodes already documents as never a type
an MIDDLE segment of java.util.Map.Entry — neither the written base (which is the full dotted text) nor a type in its own right
